difficultyRationale: Requires knowing JUnit 5's default instance lifecycle precisely, not just that lifecycle annotations exist.
prompt: A JUnit 5 test class declares a non-static instance field and does not use @TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS). By default, what is true about that field's state across the class's @Test methods?
explanation: JUnit 5's default lifecycle is PER_METHOD: a new instance of the test class is created for every @Test method. Instance fields therefore start fresh for each test and are never implicitly shared, which is also why @BeforeAll and @AfterAll must be static under the default lifecycle — they run once, before any instance exists for a specific test.

options.text: JUnit 5 creates one shared instance per test class by default, so instance fields declared without static persist across all @Test methods unless reset in @BeforeEach.
options.explanation: That behavior describes Lifecycle.PER_CLASS, which must be explicitly requested via @TestInstance; it is not the default, so relying on it without the annotation would be incorrect.

options.text: @BeforeAll and @AfterAll must be non-static because JUnit 5 instantiates the test class once per method regardless of which lifecycle method is involved.
options.explanation: Under the default per-method lifecycle it is the opposite: @BeforeAll and @AfterAll must be static precisely because they run once, before any per-test instance exists to invoke them on.

options.text: JUnit 5 creates a new test instance for each @Test method by default, so instance fields are not shared across tests.
options.explanation: This matches JUnit 5's documented default (Lifecycle.PER_METHOD): instantiation happens once per test method, so each test sees fresh, non-shared instance state.

options.text: @BeforeEach methods run once before all tests in the class, functioning the same as @BeforeAll.
options.explanation: @BeforeEach runs before every individual @Test method, not once for the whole class; conflating it with @BeforeAll describes a different annotation's behavior.

references.title: JUnit 5 User Guide — Test Instance Lifecycle
